title: Best Flooring for a Basement Remodel or ADU in Snohomish: Carpet, Vinyl or Both?
meta: Best flooring for a Snohomish basement or ADU is often both: vinyl plank where water can reach, carpet where people sleep. Wills Flooring explains zoning.
keywords: best flooring for basement remodel Snohomish, ADU flooring carpet or vinyl, carpet in a basement below grade, vinyl plank vs carpet basement, DADU flooring Snohomish WA, basement bedroom carpet

blocks.lead: For most Snohomish basements and ADUs the right answer is both: vinyl plank in the kitchenette, bath, entry and laundry, and carpet in the bedrooms and the TV room.
blocks.detail: Concrete below grade in Snohomish County is rarely bone dry, and a rental ADU takes harder use than your own upstairs. Zone the floor by how wet and how busy each room will be, then pick the specs that survive there.

blocks.html: The question usually arrives like this: "We're finishing the daylight basement on Fobes Hill for my mother-in-law" or "We're turning the shop on our Clearview acreage into a rental ADU. Carpet or vinyl?" Both are good floors. The mistake is treating the whole space as one decision. A Snohomish basement has a slab that breathes moisture, an exterior door that lets in mud, and at least one room where somebody wants to walk barefoot.

blocks.text: Start with the slab, not the sample board

items.title: Moisture test the concrete
items.text: A calcium chloride or in-slab relative humidity test tells you how much vapor is coming up through the floor. Older Snohomish slabs often have no vapor barrier under them. A high reading decides the pad and the barrier.

items.title: Look for past water
items.text: Efflorescence, a tide line on the drywall, rust on the furnace feet or a musty smell near the sump all mean water has visited. Fix the source first: gutters, grading, drain tile or a sump that actually runs.

items.title: Check flatness and cracks
items.text: Basement slabs pitch toward drains and crack along control joints. Carpet hides almost all of that. Click-lock plank does not, so low spots get patched and high spots ground before planks go down.

items.title: Plan the heat
items.text: A slab in February sits in the low 50s. Carpet and pad feel warm to bare feet. Vinyl plank feels like the slab under it unless the room has its own heat.

blocks.text: Room by room: which floor wins where

head: Room in the basement or ADU
Our usual pick
Why
rows: Mud, wet boots and dog paws come in here. Plank wipes clean; carpet at a Snohomish exterior door is brown by March.
Spills, a dishwasher line and a fridge. One leak under carpet means tearing it out.
Standing water is a certainty at some point. Carpet does not belong here.
Warmth, quiet and a soft landing for kids and older parents. Use a moisture-barrier pad below grade.
Sound absorption matters more in a concrete box than anywhere else in the house.
blocks.note: A transition strip at each doorway lets you change floors cleanly. Plan them to land under doors, not mid-hallway.

blocks.text: Price your Snohomish basement or ADU floor

blocks.html: Carpet labor below grade is published. Stretch-in over pad, on a wood subfloor or a dry slab with concrete tack strip, is $0.99 per sq ft. Glue-down straight to the concrete is $1.29. Stairs are $30 per step, there is a 500 sq ft minimum, old carpet out is $0.45 per sq ft and furniture moving $0.25. A Fobes Hill basement with two 12 by 12 bedrooms and a 20 by 16 TV room is 608 sq ft: 608 × $0.99 = $601.92 stretch-in, or 608 × $1.29 = $784.32 glued down. Vinyl plank in the wet zones is $2.50 per sq ft. Carpet, pad and plank are quoted at the estimate.

blocks.note: Labor only. Glue-down is the slab option. Carpet, pad and plank are quoted at the estimate.

blocks.text: If you carpet below grade, this is the spec that survives

items.html: Synthetic fiber only. Nylon, triexta or a good polyester. They do not hold moisture the way wool does and they do not feed mold. Nylon takes the most abuse, which matters in a rental ADU.
A moisture-barrier pad. A rebond pad with a sealed film face keeps slab vapor and small spills from soaking into the cushion. This is the single most important line on a basement carpet order.
Low, dense pile. A tight loop or short dense cut pile dries faster if something goes wrong and resists the crushing that heavy furniture on a slab causes.
Tack strip made for concrete. Regular pins pull out of old slab. Concrete-pin or adhesive strip holds the stretch for the life of the carpet.

blocks.text: If you choose vinyl plank, here is what matters underground

items.text: SPC planks stay flat over a cold slab and shrug off the swing between a heated bedroom and an unheated storage room. Thin flexible planks telegraph every slab flaw.
Many planks have an attached pad, but below grade you still want a barrier: either an attached pad rated for concrete or a separate vapor-rated underlayment. Never stack two pads.
items.note: Most plank warranties void below-grade coverage above their slab moisture limit.

items.text: Basement stairs usually stay carpeted at $30 a step, which is fine. The plank at the bottom needs a proper stair nose so the last tread is not a trip edge.

blocks.text: ADU realities: renters, noise and the county

a.title: Lean toward vinyl plank when
items: You will not see the floor between tenants
The unit's exterior door opens straight into living space
You want one floor type and fewer transitions

b.tag: Family use, aging parent, teen suite
b.title: Lean toward carpet when
items: Someone will sleep down there every night
The room above is a bedroom and you want quiet
The slab tested dry and the basement has never flooded

blocks.title: One Snohomish-specific note:
blocks.text: Many rural properties here are on well water and septic. If the ADU adds a bathroom and laundry, the sewer ejector pit usually lives in that floor. Keep hard flooring around the lid and keep it accessible.
Mistakes we pull out of Snohomish basements

items.html: Carpet straight onto the slab with a standard pad. Two winters later the pad smells and the backing has a dark bloom. A barrier pad prevents it.
Laminate in a basement. It looks like plank, but the core is wood fiber. One overflowing utility sink swells the seams for good.
Carpet in a room with a floor drain. The drain is there because someone expected water.
Finishing the floor before the framing and drywall are done. Dust and dropped screws ruin new carpet and scratch new plank. Flooring goes in last, after paint.
Get a slab moisture reading in writing. We do it at the free estimate. The number decides your pad and your plank warranty.
Draw the zones on the plan. Mark each room carpet or plank and put every transition under a door. Read our basement carpet post for what a below-grade order should say.
Ask for both samples at the same visit. Our mobile showroom brings carpet and vinyl plank boards together, so you see the carpet color next to the plank color in your own basement light.
Schedule flooring after paint and trim. Baseboards can go on before carpet if the right gap is left; for plank we set them after.
Keep the paperwork. Pad spec, plank moisture limit and our 1-year workmanship warranty go in the folder with the ADU permit.

faq.q: Is carpet a bad idea in a Snohomish basement?
faq.a: Not if the slab tests reasonably dry, the basement has never flooded, and you use a synthetic carpet on a moisture-barrier pad. Carpet is a bad idea in rooms with a floor drain, an exterior door, plumbing appliances or a history of seepage. Zone those in vinyl plank.

faq.q: Can I put vinyl plank and carpet in the same open basement room?
faq.a: Yes. A common layout runs plank from the exterior door across the kitchenette and stops at a straight line where the sitting area begins, with a flush transition. It looks intentional if the line follows a beam or a change in ceiling height.

faq.q: Do I need a vapor barrier under carpet on concrete?
faq.a: Below grade, yes. Use a rebond pad with a sealed moisture-barrier film rather than a loose plastic sheet, which bunches and traps water. If the slab reads high, we glue the carpet down at $1.29 per sq ft instead of stretching it, which removes the pad question entirely.

faq.q: Will vinyl plank be freezing cold in a Snohomish basement?
faq.a: It will feel like the slab, which sits around 50 to 55 degrees in winter. A plank with a thicker attached pad helps, and area rugs help more. Bedrooms are where carpet earns its place, at $0.99 per sq ft to install.

faq.q: Which floor is better for a rental ADU?
faq.a: Vinyl plank in most of the unit, because you cannot control pets, spills or how often it gets vacuumed. If you want one carpeted bedroom for comfort, choose a dense nylon on a barrier pad so it can be cleaned between tenants.

faq.q: Does the flooring go in before or after the ADU inspection?
faq.a: Rough inspections happen before flooring. Final inspection usually wants the finished floor in place, especially at the stairs and any egress. Schedule flooring after drywall and paint, and keep the transition and stair-nose details ready for the inspector.
